strategyPosture: Selective and patient: credit (HY OAS 3.11%, SLOOS loose) says this is rotation under a rate shock, not a rollover, so no broad de-risking — but with the 10Y at 5.24% and a hot CPI into the Oct 27-28 FOMC, new risk belongs only in the screened quality dislocations (AVGO/VRT/NOW class) after thesis verification, per the screen's own RESEARCH_SCREENED posture. Speculative nuclear stays hands-off until the unwind shows exhaustion.

themes.counterRead: The calm is real but narrow: index resilience is being carried by a shrinking set of names while the average leader is already in a double-digit drawdown. That is rotation, not health — and it flips to rollover only if credit joins in, which it has not yet. Positioning should respect the divergence rather than the index level.
themes.dataAnchor: The Mag7 averages 10.17% below its 52-week highs, an 8.57-point divergence gap versus SPY's 1.6%. The split inside the group is extreme: AAPL is only 1.3% off its high while TSLA is 26.4% off. Credit is not confirming stress — SLOOS lending standards are LOOSE at 0% (stress threshold ~40%) and HY OAS is 3.11%. The system's concentration read is ROTATION_NOT_ROLLOVER.
themes.label: Index calm masks leadership rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: The index looks fine — SPY at $769.93 sits just 1.6% below its 52-week high — so the surface story is that nothing is wrong and any dip is a buying opportunity in the same mega-cap leaders.
themes.watchFor: Divergence gap widening past -12 points, or HY OAS pushing through 3.5% — either would argue the rotation is becoming a rollover.

themes.counterRead: A hiking-cycle narrative is being priced while breakevens sit at 2.33% and spreads refuse to widen — the panic leg is ahead of the evidence. The real risk is not the CPI print itself but a term-premium accident: if the 10Y keeps climbing through the mid-5s on supply rather than expectations, duration-sensitive and leveraged balance sheets (IWM first) take the damage regardless of what the Fed does on Oct 28.
themes.dataAnchor: The rate levels are genuinely restrictive: DGS10 at 5.24%, DGS30 at 5.56%, real 10Y at 2.91%, 2s10s at +0.44. But inflation expectations are not de-anchoring — the 10Y breakeven is 2.33% — and credit is calm with HY OAS at 3.11%. VIX rose 7.4% on the day to only 16.4. Small caps are absorbing the tightening signal hardest: IWM is -7.8% over 3 months versus SPY +2.41%.
themes.label: Hot CPI puts hikes back in play — narrative running ahead of expectations data
themes.narrative: Today's September CPI printed hot (event signal HIGH, 16 headline hits) and the tape took it as a regime change: 'rate hikes are back in play' into the Oct 27-28 FOMC, with tech and long-duration assets sold first — QQQ -1.67% and IWM -1.86% on the day against SPY -1.04%.
themes.watchFor: DGS10 sustained above ~5.5% or back under 5.2% (now 5.24%); breakeven T10IE above 2.5% (now 2.33%) would confirm the narrative instead of contradicting it.

themes.counterRead: The unwind is indiscriminate within the complex, and that matters for what sits next to it: screened, revenue-producing power names are being sold in sympathy (see the quality-power divergence theme). The speculative end itself offers no data anchor for a bottom call yet — catching it here is a momentum guess, not a data trade.
themes.dataAnchor: The one-month numbers are severe: SMR -29.89%, ASTS -27.29%, OKLO -17.84%, URA -14.65%, CCJ -10.01%. These are price moves without any offsetting fundamental data in the input — no revenue inflection, no insider buying flagged for the speculative names — in a tape where the 10Y at 5.24% directly raises the discount rate on far-future cash flows.
themes.label: Speculative nuclear and space names are unwinding hard
themes.narrative: The small-nuclear / space momentum complex was sold as the purest AI-power scarcity trade; the current tape treats it as a crowded momentum unwind to exit, with another leg down today — SMR -8.94%, ASTS -9.21%, OKLO -6.99%, CCJ -4.72%.
themes.watchFor: A session where SMR/OKLO hold green while the complex is still red, or the 10Y back under 5.2% — the first signs the unwind is exhausting rather than compounding.

themes.counterRead: Data-ahead does not mean buyable today: the same rate tape that created the dislocation can deepen it into the Oct 27-28 FOMC, and several of these names carry earnings windows before any re-rating can be confirmed. The edge here is preparation — verified theses and levels ready — rather than chasing the first green day.
themes.dataAnchor: The fundamentals of the quality end point the other way. AVGO is the screen's top conviction name (score 81, Tier A): revenue +55% YoY, 67.8% gross margin, $26.9B FCF at a 42.1% FCF margin — with the stock 29.9% below its high at RSI 42.6. VRT is 41.4% below its high with revenue +27.7% YoY and $1.89B FCF. NOW shows revenue growing 23.1% YoY (recovery confirmed) at 27.6% below its high. APP is 64.3% below its high at RSI 31.1 with a 60.8% FCF margin. The screen classifies these declines as SENTIMENT_DRIVEN, not fundamental.
themes.label: Quality AI infrastructure: fundamentals running ahead of price
themes.narrative: The broad story is that AI infrastructure is a bubble deflating with the rate shock — AVGO -2.71% today, the whole complex marked down together, and the dislocations screen reads 26 names down 20-78% from their highs.
themes.watchFor: AVGO holding its post-CPI low while QQQ makes new lows (relative-strength flip), or any of these names reclaiming its 20-day average on volume — the signal that the dislocation is closing rather than widening.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is the opportunity and the trap at the same time: VST's revenue inflection is flagged DETERIORATING in the opportunity screen even as the growth data prints positive, so the quality case rests on cash flow and insider behavior, not momentum. If the complex keeps unwinding, quality gets cheaper before it gets vindicated — sizing has to assume another leg down in sympathy.
themes.dataAnchor: VST's data does not match the speculative end: revenue +19.1% YoY, FCF $1.32B, P/S 2.9x, and insiders bought $1.17M at the trough, with the stock 29.8% below its high but still +7.7% on a one-month trend and RSI 53.1 — a pullback in an intact trend, not a collapse. BWXT shows the same pattern on the nuclear-supply side: revenue +26.1% YoY (recovery confirmed) at 43.6% below its high, RSI 38.8. Both are flagged FULL_SIGNAL / SENTIMENT_DRIVEN by the screen.
themes.label: Quality power diverges from the nuclear unwind
themes.narrative: Power exposure is being sold as one trade — VST fell 6.05% today alongside the nuclear complex — implying the whole AI-power theme is deflating at once.
themes.watchFor: VST decoupling from SMR/OKLO on a red day for the complex, or follow-through insider buying — either confirms the divergence is being priced.

watchFor: DGS10 weekly close above ~5.5% (escalation) or back under 5.2% (relief) — currently 5.24%
10Y breakeven (T10IE) above 2.5% — currently 2.33%; a break higher validates the hiking narrative
HY OAS widening through 3.5% from 3.11% — credit confirming stress would flip rotation to rollover
Mag7-vs-SPY 52-week-high divergence gap widening past -12 points from -8.57
VIX sustained above 20 — currently 16.4 despite a +7.4% day
whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds around the Oct 27-28 FOMC and the long end: if the 10Y pushes through the mid-5s with breakevens rising from 2.33%, rotation turns to rollover and IWM (-7.8% over 3 months) leads down; if yields stall, the snapback concentrates in the washed-out quality AI-infrastructure and power names whose revenue never broke.
